facts.fact: mHealth Africa (TICANALYSE) states that its mHealth community platform automatically transmits community-collected data (consultations, vaccinations, input management) to the national DHIS2 (SIGSANTE) through synchronisation mechanisms using HL7 FHIR and secure APIs, so two systems exchange data.

systems.owner: Health Information Directorate, Ministry of Health

note: as_of is the document's published date; it gives no date for when the synchronisation began.

note: States the handover of 380 smartphones and 270 tablets on 2026-08-28 to extend the mHealth community-health platform to Gontougo; says nothing about data exchange between systems.

facts.fact: The Council of Ministers of 10 July 2024 adopted a decree making the Couverture maladie universelle registration number the health identifier in all public and private health facilities, replacing any other number for the patient file, care and referencing of the patient's health data across facilities' information systems, with 24 months for users and facilities to comply; the document reports adoption of the decree, not use in service.
facts.system: CMU registration number as health identifier

facts.fact: The Ministry of Health piloted the mHealth.ci community health platform in five districts of the Poro region from December 2024 (full operational launch 8 January 2025), and the authors state it integrates with the national health information system DHIS2.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health (DSCPS, DIS, DISD) with UNICEF
systems.tiers: community health workers; frontline health workers

facts.fact: The authors, from interviews in June 2023, state that although the three outbreak surveillance tools (DHIS2, MAGPI and SORMAS) are designed to allow interoperability, there is no data exchange and consolidation presently in place between them.

The authors state that MAGPI is the only surveillance system in Côte d'Ivoire currently linked with the laboratories where samples are analysed (SORMAS has the function but it was not used), per interviews in June 2023.

systems.owner: Direction de l'Informatique et de l'Information Sanitaire (Ministry of Health)

systems.tiers: pilot in 2 regions and 11 districts, from July-August 2021 to June 2023

note: A workshop report on a technical architecture and a pooled database concept; no exchange is contracted, piloted or in service.

facts.fact: Ecofin Agency reports that, according to the Health Ministry, Cote d'Ivoire is progressively establishing a national interoperability platform for its health information systems to exchange data securely.

note: Document names interoperability between the platforms as the critical challenge now; no exchange stated in service or under way.
